description: Step through the matrix multiplications and activation vector calculations that transform inputs into predictions.

slides.title: Vectorized Forward Propagation 🚀
slides.content:
# Forward Propagation with Matrices

Modern deep learning hardware (GPUs and TPUs) executes forward passes using high-speed matrix multiplications:

For layer $l$:
$$
\mathbf{Z}^{[l]} = \mathbf{W}^{[l]} \mathbf{A}^{[l-1]} + \mathbf{b}^{[l]}
$$
$$
\mathbf{A}^{[l]} = \sigma(\mathbf{Z}^{[l]})
$$

* **$\mathbf{A}^{[l-1]}$:** Activations from preceding layer (where $\mathbf{A}^{[0]} = \mathbf{X}$, the input batch).
* **$\mathbf{W}^{[l]}$:** Weight matrix connecting layer $l-1$ to layer $l$.
* **$\mathbf{b}^{[l]}$:** Bias vector for layer $l$.
* **$\sigma$:** Non-linear element-wise activation function.

slides.title: Vectorized Forward Pass in Python 🐍
slides.content: Here is how a 2-layer network computes predictions on a sample feature vector:
slides.codeSnippet:
import math

def relu(x: float) -> float:
    return max(0.0, x)

# Input vector: 2 features
x = [1.5, -0.5]
# Hidden layer: 2 neurons (weights: 2x2, biases: 2)
w1 = [[0.8, -0.2], [0.5, 0.9]]
b1 = [0.1, -0.1]

# Compute hidden activations
h1 = relu(x[0]*w1[0][0] + x[1]*w1[0][1] + b1[0])
h2 = relu(x[0]*w1[1][0] + x[1]*w1[1][1] + b1[1])
print('Hidden layer activations:', [round(h1, 3), round(h2, 3)])
